text:
A keloid is a raised, firm scar that grows beyond the boundaries of the original wound or injury, caused by excessive collagen (mainly type I and III) production during healing. Unlike hypertrophic scars, it doesn't regress on its own and tends to recur after simple excision. It's more common in people with darker skin and often appears on the earlobes, chest, shoulders, and upper back.

CONFIDENCE: 97
